slides.title: Three Views of One Memory
slides.takeaway: Distinct views of memory; never add them together.

data.caption: Windows sees about 64 GB; GPU budget 64,000 MiB

slides.notes: 128 GB is installed. Windows reports about 64 GB visible, and nvidia-smi reports a 64,000 MiB GPU memory budget. These are different views of the same memory, not additive, and this is not dedicated VRAM.

slides.title: Memory Views Are Like Map Zoom
slides.takeaway: Same territory, different viewers; totals never stack.
slides.notes: Think of one city with several maps. A driver and a courier each see part of it. Adding their maps would double-count streets, just as adding memory views overstates capacity.

slides.title: Measured Single-Stream Decode
slides.takeaway: MoE coder decodes fast enough for interactive coding.

data.caption: Local-AI-Bench, Oct 2026, shared machine; not a spec

slides.notes: Qwen3-Coder 30B at about 86 tokens per second with 0.13 second time to first token. Measured on this shared machine in October 2026; treat as observed, not guaranteed.

slides.title: Concurrency for Shared Teams
slides.takeaway: Aggregate throughput rises when streams run concurrently.
slides.notes: Aggregate numbers across concurrent streams, measured on a shared machine. They indicate headroom, not a guarantee or device comparison.

slides.title: MoE Is a Specialist Clinic
slides.takeaway: Only a few experts work per token, so decode runs faster.
slides.notes: Qwen3-Coder 30B activates about 3B parameters per token. Dense Qwen3.6 27B uses all weights each token, about 13 tokens per second. MoE decodes several times faster at similar size.

slides.title: Model Sizing Bands
slides.takeaway: Bands guide planning; bigger is not a claim of accuracy.
slides.notes: S 1-4B, M 7-8B, L 14-20B, XL 24-32B. These are planning estimates for memory and speed, not accuracy tiers.

slides.title: Hybrid Routing Architecture
slides.takeaway: Sensitive work stays local; heaviest reasoning can go cloud.

elements.label: CAD/PLM and source IP stay on the local lane

slides.notes: The router sends sensitive, frequent tasks like code generation and RAG over internal docs to the local lane. The heaviest reasoning can route to cloud models when appropriate.

slides.title: Local Codegen and RAG Loop
slides.takeaway: Internal docs ground local code answers on device.
slides.notes: Retrieval pulls from internal engineering docs, then the local coder model generates. Runtimes: llama.cpp build 11573 native ARM64 with CUDA, and Foundry Local with the CUDA execution provider.
